evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.5.27: sē praebēbat patientem atque impigrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “Not lazy” (in- + piger), so active and untiring.

evidence: Cic. Att. 10.16.6: tē vegetum nōbīs in Graeciā siste (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of someone fresh and in good health, an old person still active, troops not yet tired.

evidence: Cato Agr. praef. 3: mercātor strēnuus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of energetic people, often in war or business; also brave.

evidence: Sen. Ep. 95.10: philosophia et contemplātīva est et āctīva (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A term of the philosophers and grammarians, the active life and the active voice; not used of a busy or energetic person.

phrases.latin: tē vegetum nōbīs in Graeciā siste
phrases.english: be there for us in Greece in good form
he showed himself patient and tireless

phrases.latin: Avus octōgintā annōs nātus etiamnunc vegetus est.
phrases.english: Grandpa is eighty and still very active.
